purpose: Feasibility probe: use the local PaddleOCR baseline (PaddleOCR-VL-1.6) to determine a page's physical text range when importing a new page, so that continuation drafts are auto-trimmed to the page boundary (删头去尾) instead of dumping the host entry's full remaining text for manual trimming. Ground truth = the proofread (初校) @333 .gj. Probe only — no production code changed; OCR used strictly as a range ruler, never as a text source.

method.ocr: paddleocr-baseline service (FastAPI, port 8010) → PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 cloud provider, single job, cold start ~40s
comparison: candidate: what add --page 333 would import = 中's remaining 16 paragraphs (464 chars)
alignment: difflib.SequenceMatcher on normalized text; trim point = end of last matching block against the candidate

results.auto_trim: 377 chars vs proofread 376 — 1 char apart; first-15 and last-15 chars identical (能爲役杜預註：… / …邈私飮沈醉趙)
results.draft_reduction: candidate 464 → 377 chars (19% overflow to next page removed)

diff_breakdown.variant_forms: 9 (鄕/鄉 尚/尙 郞/郎 飮/飲 日/曰 興/與 etc.) — irrelevant to range detection
diff_breakdown.bracket_loss: OCR emits no 【】 frame characters — range use unaffected, but OCR cannot be a text source

conclusion: Feasible and worth implementing: draft text stays sourced from the sqlite transcription (faithful); OCR only fixes the cut point via the same difflib-tolerant alignment already used by continuation_from_prev. Residual proofreading reduces to verifying the head/tail joint at ±1 char. Limitations recorded: vertical woodblock without ruling is an easy case for the VL model; one OCR job per added page (~40s cold + provider latency); OCR must never feed gold text.
artifacts: OCR raw result kept at /tmp/kx-ocr-test/out/0333.{md,json} (ephemeral); scripts unchanged
note: OCR token for the probe was read from local-only reflog commit 150cf35 and passed via env var; never written to any tracked file.
